desc:
Decide whether the integer array nums can be cut into three non-empty contiguous parts (a prefix, a middle block and a suffix) whose sums are all equal. Return true if such a cut exists and false otherwise.

Values may be negative or zero.

[0, 2, 1, -6, 6, -7, 9, 1, 2, 0, 1]  -> true   ([0,2,1] [-6,6,-7,9,1] [2,0,1], each sums to 3)
[1, 2, 3, 4]                         -> false
hints: If the three parts each sum to s, what must the sum of the whole array be?
The total must be divisible by 3 and each part must sum to total / 3. Walk through the array, accumulating a running sum.

Every time the running sum reaches the target, count one finished part and restart the running sum at 0. If you finish three parts before the array ends (or exactly at the end), the answer is yes; with a total of 0 you may even finish more than three, which is fine.
editorial: The total S must be divisible by 3, and each part has to sum to t = S / 3. Scan from the left with a running sum; whenever it equals t, close a part and reset the running sum to 0. If at least three parts get closed, we can merge any extra ones: the first part closed, the second part closed, and everything after as the third part. That last block sums to S - 2t = t and it is not empty because a third part was closed at or after its start.

The case S = 0 works with the same code: t = 0 and each zero-sum stretch closes a part. Negative numbers do not break anything because we only compare against the exact target, never prune on size. Time is O(n) and space O(1).
